question: Nursing informatics is a blend of nursing practice and which other two major fields?
explanation: You've got this! Nursing informatics simply brings together nursing science, computer science, and information science to help us manage health data smoothly. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the main reason we use informatics tools in our daily nursing practice?

options.A: Improve patient safety and care delivery
options.B: Eliminate the need for nursing documentation

explanation: Think about why we love tech in the ward—it helps make our work smoother, cuts down mistakes, and keeps our patients safer! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h1)

question: In a hospital, what do we mean when we talk about a 'WOW'?
explanation: A WOW is just those handy mobile computer carts you push around the ward to check records right beside the patient's bed. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why do nurses love using mobile computer carts (WOWs) right at the bedside?

options.A: To replace traditional bedside drug trolleys entirely
options.B: To allow patients to browse the internet
options.C: To document care immediately and reduce errors
options.D: To store heavy surgical equipment securely

explanation: Charting right away means you don't have to rely on memory at the end of a long, tiring shift. It saves time and stops mistakes! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the modern digital replacement for the traditional paper patient chart?
explanation: An EHR is simply the digital folder that holds a patient's complete medical history and treatment notes in one safe place. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h3)

question: How does scanning barcodes before giving medications help keep patients safe?

options.A: It automatically calculates the correct drug dosage
options.B: It prevents nurses from working overtime shifts
options.C: It replaces the need for verbal physician orders
options.D: It verifies the right patient and drug before administration

explanation: It acts as a quick safety double-check! Scanning the wristband and drug package ensures the right medication goes to the right patient every time. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the main job of a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS)?

options.A: To provide alerts and evidence-based guidance to clinicians
options.B: To automatically diagnose and treat patients without staff
options.C: To schedule nursing shifts and manage payroll
options.D: To track hospital equipment inventory in real time

explanation: Think of CDSS as a helpful assistant on the computer that pops up with useful reminders, guidelines, and warnings to guide your care. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h4)

question: You see a sudden drug-allergy warning pop up on your computer screen. What system is hard at work here?
explanation: That pop-up is a classic CDSS feature designed to catch allergies and prevent medication errors before they happen. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h4)

question: In healthcare technology, what does the abbreviation 'RPM' stand for?
explanation: RPM means keeping an eye on patient vitals using connected devices even when the patient is resting comfortably at home. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is remote patient monitoring so helpful for patients managing long-term (chronic) illnesses?

options.A: It catches warning signs early before emergencies develop
options.B: It completely removes the need for in-person doctor visits
options.C: It lowers the cost of hospital building construction
options.D: It allows patients to prescribe their own medications

explanation: By tracking daily stats from afar, nurses can spot little changes early and step in before a small issue becomes an emergency. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h5)

question: What happens when nurses start ignoring computer warnings because there are simply too many minor pop-ups?
explanation: Just like the boy who cried wolf, too many unnecessary buzzers and pop-ups make staff tune them out—which is dangerous if a real emergency warning sounds! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which of these simple habits is best for keeping patient data safe when using hospital computers?

options.A: Sharing your login password with nursing students
options.B: Writing access codes on sticky notes near the monitor
options.C: Leaving patient charts open on the public desk
options.D: Logging off the workstation when stepping away

explanation: Always lock or log off your screen when you walk away. Patient privacy is a core nursing duty! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h6)
